newsitem.title: TURKEY: Greek foreign minister to visit Turkey for meeting.
newsitem.headline: Greek foreign minister to visit Turkey for meeting.

text.p: Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos will attend a conference in Istanbul on Wednesday, a day after announcing Greece would maintain its veto on European Union aid to Turkey, a consulate official said.
Pangalos was to attend a meeting of ministers from the Black Sea Economic Cooperation group.
"He is arriving at 12.55 p.m. (0955 GMT) and is to attend the meeting of ministers," a spokesman at the Greek consulate in Istanbul told Reuters.
Pangalos said at a meeting of EU ministers in Luxembourg on Tuesday that Greece could not agree to unblock aid worth 375 million ecus ($424 million) over a dispute with Turkey in the Aegean.
"We have repeatedly declared that we cannot accept Turkish behaviour vis-a-vis our sovereignty," he told a news conference.
The veto dashed hopes Athens would ease its stance against its rival. Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said the move was disappointing.
The aid has been promised to help Ankara meet the increased competition posed by the customs union with the EU which took effect in January 1996.

Despite the veto, EU officials reported some progress. Greece and Turkey formally agreed an approach to solving differences in the Aegean, where they almost came to blows last year over some uninhabited islets.
Pangalos was scheduled to leave Turkey early on Wednesday evening.
